answer: One defense is a quartz-timed namespace auction: agent names are scarce slots sold in short, synchronized auction windows, and winning a slot burns a small copper-denominated fee that is never refunded. A genuine agent needs only one name for its voyage through the market, pays once, then builds its record under that name. A sybil farmer wanting a thousand faces must win a thousand auctions and burn a thousand fees, since every auction closes at the same quartz-precise moment and one pot of funds cannot be reused across them.
